title: Recommendations to guide sampling effort for polygon-based participatory mapping used to identify perceived ecosystem services hotspots
author: Carrie, Stringer, et al.

steps.title: Scope study area and pilot
steps.instruction: Conduct focus groups and transect walks to define the mangrove system boundary, develop a standardized list of ecosystem services to map, identify local landmarks for quality control, and pilot questionnaire language and mapping approach (including point vs polygon) with 30 households.

steps.title: Define representative sample
steps.instruction: Select the three villages adjacent to the coastline (out of nine) and randomly choose households by picking every nth house from village lists, sampling 150 households (≈16 % of households in each village) to balance representativeness, resources, and the ≥25‑participant recommendation.

steps.title: Administer household questionnaire
steps.instruction: Give each selected household a laminated colour map at 1:15 000 scale (downloaded from Google Earth) and a face‑to‑face questionnaire; first check map literacy by having respondents locate their home and local landmarks, exclude the three households unable to do so, then ask respondents to draw polygons (no limit on number, size or shape) around areas they consider important for each ecosystem service.

steps.title: Disaggregate sample into groups
steps.instruction: Analyse adaptive‑capacity data using non‑linear principal component analysis followed by cluster analysis on the component scores to create three a‑priori groups: accumulating households, coping households, and flexible households.

steps.title: Digitise annotated maps
steps.instruction: Using ArcMap version 10.4, digitise the 628 polygons from the 147 annotated maps, organise them by ecosystem‑service attribute and adaptive‑capacity group in a file geodatabase, and store each attribute‑group combination as a separate feature class.

steps.title: Calculate mapping rates and overlap
steps.instruction: For each ecosystem‑service‑group combination, compute the mapping rate as (number of polygons ÷ number of participants who drew polygons); observed rates ranged from 1.0 to 1.38 polygons per participant. Identify occasions where fewer than 25 participants drew polygons (26 of 36 occasions) and note that only the service “protection from storms and erosion” reached ≥25 participants in all three groups. Exclude any polygons covering >50 % of the total study area before overlap analysis.

steps.title: Decide on further mapping or proceed
steps.instruction: If spatial agreement (polygon overlap) is low, consider additional mapping (step 7); otherwise, continue to hotspot generation. In this study, proceed with disaggregated analysis focusing on the four services most important to all groups (protection from storms and erosion, food, sediment accumulation, habitat provisioning) and add interview questions to triangulate especially low‑overlap services such as food.

steps.title: Generate ecosystem‑service hotspots
steps.instruction: Create hotspot layers by counting polygon overlaps and applying two cut‑off thresholds: the top 67 % and the top 90 % of overlap values for each service‑group combination.

steps.title: Triangulate with narrative data
steps.instruction: Analyse narrative information collected from focus groups, open‑ended survey questions, and semi‑structured interviews (structured around each household’s annotated map) to identify specific features at hotspot locations, explain differences between groups (e.g., presence of aquaculture ponds for habitat provisioning), and increase confidence in hotspot interpretation.
